timeline.phase: 1e. Direct power-mean tree calculus with marked perturbations (sec 1, p3, L118-123) [FINAL FRAME]
timeline.approach: Work directly with iterated power means and tilted path transitions; marked perturbations specify where replicas branch; the change of density gives signed coefficients for extending an old replica tree. Two-replica identity found; higher products problematic.
timeline.why_abandoned: (sub-branch) coefficients alternate in sign, dummy anchors cancel, conditional projections not admissible as test functions.

timeline.phase: 1f. Target: conditional decorrelation; the small-gap division problem (sec 1, p3, L124-128)
timeline.approach: Target conditional decorrelation of sitewise product vectors, then ordinary multioverlap concentration. Fresh subtrees isolate conditional moments; coarse partitions; equal-exponent refinements.
timeline.why_abandoned: Recovering a prescribed shape divides by products of small exponent gaps; continuity errors too large after division.

timeline.phase: 2a. Pinning again; exact purity; factorial-polynomial + two-copy cancellation (sec 2, p3, L130-134)
timeline.approach: Retry pinning; claim exact purity inside a strict exponent jump; factorial-polynomial expansions and a two-copy cancellation.
timeline.why_abandoned: Pinning observation law incompatible with cavity comparison; hidden Poisson-Dirichlet clustering refutes exact purity; signed identities still do not give the covariance estimate.

timeline.phase: 2b. Shift of branching depths (sec 2, p3, L135-140) [DECISIVE PIVOT]
timeline.approach: Shift every internal branching depth of the target tree by one level, so shifted splits avoid the old tree's branching depths and each new branching vertex pays a small fresh-divergence factor that matches the normalization.
timeline.verbatim_excerpt: Great! Need carefully prove average error little with shifted depths not rare

timeline.phase: 2c. Induction, anchor identity, martingale averaging, marker anchor, order of limits (sec 2, p3, L141-146)
timeline.approach: Induct by replacing proper descendant groups with conditional means; an anchor identity gives a positive weighted sum of squared replacement differences; bounded martingale increments control shifts on average over depths; a marker anchor converts conditional decorrelation into ordinary multioverlap concentration; N-limit before L-limit.

timeline.phase: 2d. Logarithmic expansion; upper bound; perturbation selection and polarization (sec 2, p3-4, L147-156)
timeline.approach: Power-mean expansion organized by adding paths, telescoping coefficient magnitudes, geometric remainder; upper bound normalized by the all-plus interaction value with the even-power convexity remainder; sublinear marked Poisson perturbations with diagonal selection; polarization.

timeline.phase: 2e. Comparison with independent trial messages (sec 2, p4, L157-162)
timeline.approach: A uniformly sampled site's leaf magnetization defines trial messages through arctanh and successive conditional laws; empirical spin-pattern probabilities are replaced by independent trial-label probabilities; exceptional shapes, large insertion counts and series tails removed in sequence.

timeline.phase: 3a. Checks: subtree law, coefficients, charging, martingale (sec 3, p4, L164-172)
timeline.approach: Check target-subtree law when the anchor is in the old tree (marginalization); check coefficients at two levels and reorganize as a positive squared-difference identity; charge distinct vertices even at coinciding depths; martingale bound along unary stretches.

timeline.phase: 3b. Background-measure concern; Palm formulation (sec 3, p4, L173-177)
timeline.approach: Concern that varying the insertion parameter changes the background measure; fix: each value is a hypothetical extra factor in a fixed background supplied by Poisson removal; anchor factor cancels; uniform analytic estimates; polarized marks.

timeline.phase: 3c. Joint check of induction and marker anchor; cavity comparison (sec 3, p4, L178-183)
timeline.approach: Three-copy estimate for the normalized squared conditional covariance; fresh copy vs original shape; fresh uniformly sampled sites and expectations; finite cutoffs.

timeline.phase: 3d. Reduction to first moments and final claim (sec 3, p4, L184-188)
timeline.approach: Subtract the all-plus interaction value, truncate interaction and field, remove truncations with uniform error bounds; claim the lower comparison matches the upper bound.

detailed.description: Structural route: Panchenko's finite-RSB spin-distribution identification + pair-overlap ultrametricity
detailed.conflict: missing estimate (pair overlaps do not determine multioverlaps)

lesson.obstruction: Panchenko's finite-RSB analysis [4] identifies the hierarchical spin distribution only for finite-RSB asymptotic Gibbs measures (of perturbed models). Ultrametricity of PAIR overlaps, which Ghirlanda-Guerra-type identities give, does not determine the MULTIoverlaps R_S = N^-1 sum_i prod_{a in S} sigma_i^a. In a diluted model the cavity insertion depends on all of them, so the structural route leaves a gap: one must also show that general states are approximated by finite-RSB ones.
lesson.lesson_statement: The object to control is the full family of finite multioverlaps on prescribed replica trees, not pair-overlap ultrametricity (C1).
lesson.summary_excerpt: pair-overlap ultrametricity alone does not determine the multioverlaps
lesson.generality: general (rules out every route through pair-overlap structure alone for diluted models)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known. Panchenko, 'Spin glass models from the point of view of spin distributions', Ann. Probab. 41 (2013) shows the diluted-model state is a spin distribution governed by all multioverlaps. The final paper (intro) repeats this point and cites Pan13; the trace does not cite Pan13.
lesson.salvage: The multioverlap R_S becomes the basic observable (paper eq. tree:multioverlap); Panchenko's hierarchical representation idea survives as the target shape of the trial law (comp:encoding).
lesson.influence: decisive for the target: it defines b4.3 (concentrate all multioverlaps on prescribed trees) and the comparison c2 (empirical pattern probabilities are combinations of multioverlaps).
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The trace never says how to bridge from ultrametric pair structure to multioverlaps. It drops the 'identify the physical Gibbs structure' programme entirely and later builds the hierarchy into the construction (PV2). The paper says so explicitly: no ultrametric organization of the physical Gibbs states is assumed.

detailed.outcome: abandoned (restart to PROVE2): none yields one

lesson.summary_excerpt: Initial checks look for a counterexample in the assumptions
lesson.generality: local (sanity probes, not a proof of anything)

lesson.correctness: correct as far as reported (absence of a counterexample proves nothing, and the model treats it that way: it moves on)

detailed.description: Many-site cavity argument: condition on randomness shared by all sites in a hierarchical representation, then seek independent site messages
detailed.conflict: other (shared randomness adapts to the sampled sites)

lesson.obstruction: A many-site cavity argument conditions on randomness shared by all sites in a hierarchical representation and looks for independent site messages. But the shared randomness can ADAPT to the sampled sites (selection/overfitting). A pointwise law of large numbers gives no uniform comparison over the adaptive choice (b1.1). Pinning may select states with the wrong weights (b1.2).
lesson.lesson_statement: Conditioning on shared hierarchical randomness gives no independent messages, because the conditioning variable can depend on the sites being tested. Control must be uniform over prescribed shapes, or the sites must be fresh and uniformly sampled (C4). The VERBATIM 'Aha' records a related realization (C6): a sufficiently flexible shared variable can encode the original model at a smaller scale, so conditioning on it is not a simplification.
lesson.verbatim_excerpt: Aha recursive structure: overfitting shared variable can simulate original model at smaller scale.
lesson.summary_excerpt: this shared randomness can adapt to the sampled sites
lesson.generality: general for this class (any argument that conditions on an unconstrained shared variable)
lesson.known_in_literature: Partly known: the cavity comparison of Aizenman-Sims-Starr (ASS03) and Panchenko's spin-distribution approach (Pan13, Sec. 2.2) use uniformly random sites and exchangeability rather than conditioning on shared randomness. The adaptivity obstruction is a standard concern but not a named result.
lesson.salvage: Fresh uniformly sampled sites + expectations over the trial hierarchy (c2 L157-159, v7 L181-182; paper Lemma comp:encoding uses an independent uniform site i in [N] in the root, and comp:patterns).
lesson.influence: contributory: shapes the design of the comparison (c2) and of the target (b4.3)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The 'Aha' line is ambiguous. It could mean (i) an obstruction (the shared variable can simulate the model, so conditioning is vacuous) or (ii) a constructive hint (the hierarchy has a recursive, self-similar structure that a smaller-scale system can reproduce, cf. the N vs N+1 reservoir). The summary goes straight on to 'auxiliary hierarchies'. Reading (ii) would make it a seed of PV2.

detailed.conflict: other (pinning selects states with the wrong weights)

lesson.obstruction: Pinning a few spins (in the style of the pinning lemma) to make the measure nearly product may select states with the wrong (non-Gibbs, non-cavity) weights.

detailed.description: Poisson perturbations motivated by the Barbier-Panchenko multioverlap identities [1] (Bayesian setting)
detailed.conflict: no transport mechanism (posterior-sampled vs fractionally weighted observations have different laws)

lesson.obstruction: Barbier-Panchenko's multioverlap identities [1] come from revealing noisy observations in Bayes-optimal inference. There the revealed observation is a posterior sample (Nishimori property). In the spin-glass power-mean hierarchy the analogous object is a FRACTIONALLY WEIGHTED observation, i.e. tilted by exponents m_d. Its law differs, so the Bayesian identities do not transfer.
lesson.lesson_statement: Identities must be derived directly from the iterated power means and their tilted path transitions, not imported from the Nishimori setting (C8).
lesson.summary_excerpt: The Bayesian setting does not transfer automatically
lesson.known_in_literature: Known in spirit: Nishimori identities are specific to Bayes-optimal (planted) models (Barbier-Panchenko 2022; Nishimori 1981). The specific comparison (posterior-sampled vs fractionally weighted) is the model's own formulation.
lesson.salvage: Poisson perturbations survive (marked, sublinear; b4, b4.5). The paper's Palm/add-one identity (pert:palm) plays the role the Nishimori identity plays in BP.
lesson.influence: decisive for the frame: the next sentence starts the final route ("therefore works directly with iterated power means")
lesson.what_was_not_learned: n/a

detailed.description: Extend the identity directly to higher products of replicas
detailed.conflict: missing estimate (alternating signs, dummy-anchor cancellation, projections not admissible as test functions)

lesson.obstruction: For products of more than two replicas, the signed extension coefficients alternate in sign, contributions from dummy anchors cancel, and conditional projections cannot be inserted as arbitrary test functions, because the test must be fixed as the insertion varies and must live on the old tree.
lesson.lesson_statement: Signed higher-order identities alone give no estimate. One needs (a) a positive (squared) form, (b) tests that are fixed functions of the old tree, and (c) control of the ABSOLUTE coefficient sum (C9).
lesson.summary_excerpt: Higher products are harder: their coefficients alternate in sign
lesson.generality: general within this method (any GG/stochastic-stability-type identity with signed coefficients)
lesson.known_in_literature: Partly known: alternating signs in higher-order stochastic-stability identities are familiar (Aizenman-Contucci 1998; Barra-De Sanctis 2007 for diluted multioverlaps), but these are cited only in the paper.
lesson.salvage: Canceled-anchor expansion (paper Lemma tree:extension-expansion: H fixed as insertion parameters vary); old-tree polynomial tests f (Thm pert:tree-identity); absolute-coefficient bounds (Lemma tree:charging).
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The obstruction 'projections cannot be inserted as test functions' is only resolved in section 3 (v1: marginalizing unused paths allows conditional covariance estimates even for correlated observables).

detailed.description: Fresh subtrees isolate conditional moments; recover the prescribed shape by dividing by products of small exponent gaps
detailed.conflict: missing estimate (continuity errors too large after division)

lesson.obstruction: Fresh subtrees isolate useful conditional moments. But recovering a whole prescribed tree shape S requires dividing by its normalizing coefficient, a product of small exponent gaps (paper: kappa(S) = prod_v prod_j (m_{d_v} - j m_{d_v+1}), with a factor -delta per branching vertex). The available continuity errors do not carry that small factor, so after division they blow up. Coarse partitions of the exponent grid and equal-exponent refinements hit the same problem.
lesson.lesson_statement: Errors must carry the same small factor as the normalizer: one needs a RELATIVE absolute-coefficient bound, (sum |c_E|)/|normalizer| <= C (C10).
lesson.summary_excerpt: available continuity errors are too large after that division
lesson.generality: general within the method (rules out every partition or refinement scheme that leaves error coefficients unmatched)
lesson.known_in_literature: Not known as a named obstacle. It is internal to the model's tree calculus. Small-denominator issues in stochastic-stability identities are folklore.
lesson.correctness: correct (confirmed by the paper's need for eq. decor:relative-absolute-cost)
lesson.salvage: The requirement itself is salvaged and becomes the design specification of the shift (b4.3.7) and of Lemma tree:charging.
lesson.influence: decisive: the shift is introduced as the answer to exactly this requirement ("matching the small factor in the prescribed shape's normalization", L136-137)
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The summary does not say whether the model first tried to improve the continuity estimates themselves (e.g. rates) before changing the target trees.

detailed.description: Exact purity claim inside a strict exponent jump

lesson.obstruction: An exact purity claim (that within one level of the hierarchy the overlaps are constant, so a finite hierarchy captures everything exactly) is too strong. Hidden Poisson-Dirichlet clustering inside a strict exponent jump m_d < m_{d+1} can keep nontrivial overlap variation that the finite grid does not resolve.
lesson.lesson_statement: Only approximate concentration can be expected, and only after the hierarchy is refined (L -> infinity after N -> infinity) and averaged over branching depths (C11).
lesson.summary_excerpt: An exact purity claim also proves too strong
lesson.generality: general (rules out exact finite-level purity for every finite grid)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known: Ruelle probability cascades (Ruelle 1987) and Poisson-Dirichlet weights within a level; full-RSB structure (Talagrand 2011; Panchenko 2013 book). Ruelle87 is cited in the paper, not the trace.
lesson.salvage: Averaging over depths (paper Thm decor:overlap-concentration is stated for A_{L,eta} averages) and the order of limits (Remark decor:order-of-limits).
lesson.influence: necessary: it forces the 'on average over branching depths' formulation that the paper's introduction singles out

pivots.new_idea: Delay (shift) every internal branching depth of the target tree by one level (S -> S^+). The shifted target splits cannot coincide with branching depths of the old tree, so each must be created by a fresh unary split with coefficient m_{e+1} - m_{e+2} = -delta. The absolute coefficient sum then carries one delta per target vertex, exactly matching the normalizer J = kappa(S^+)^2 ~ delta^{2b}; this gives the relative bound (sum |c_E|)/|J| <= C_{k,eta}. The shift is undone afterwards on average over depths (PV6).

L2 = approach family inside a strategy, identified by its central tool or invariant. A summary paragraph that changes the central tool opens a new L2 node. A revisit of an earlier family gets a new node whose clauses_applied point to the earlier lesson.

L3+ = a technical variant, sub-construction or lemma attempted inside an approach. Assign L3+ only when the summary presents the step as a refinement of the current approach ('then', 'pursues', 'replaced', 'returning to', 'further', 'the change is').

CONFLICT is recorded only where the summary states a failure. A node that fails only because all its children failed is 'abandoned (children failed)' and has no conflict of its own. A node left without a stated reason is 'abandoned (left open)', and its backtrack trigger is 'unclear'.

Backtrack = the next node in trace order is not a child of the current failing node. Distance d = level(failing node) - (level(next node) - 1). d=1 is a sibling; d>=2 is a backjump; next node at L1 is a restart.
Trigger type: conflict if the left node has a stated failure; insight if the left branch was viable but bypassed by a simpler new idea (subsumption); unclear otherwise.

Learned clause = a stated reason for failure phrased as a reusable constraint. Reuse = a later node whose stated reason or design cites or embodies it (explicit if the summary links it, inferred otherwise; see notes).
Length = words of the summary text from the node's first line up to the first line of the next node outside its subtree (page headers excluded). Line boundaries are approximate (+-1 line).

nodes.description: Problem: prove or disprove lim F_N = inf_r Phi_r (Mezard-Parisi / Panchenko-Talagrand sharpness conjecture) for diluted even-p Ising models with PT factorization and positivity
Strategy PROVE (first entry): close the gap between the PT interpolation upper bound [5] and the missing lower bound, starting from the structural (finite-RSB) route of Panchenko [4]

lesson.obstruction: Panchenko's finite-RSB analysis [4] identifies the hierarchical spin distribution only for finite-RSB asymptotic Gibbs measures (of perturbed models). Ultrametricity of PAIR overlaps, which Ghirlanda-Guerra-type identities give, does not determine the MULTIoverlaps R_S = N^-1 sum_i prod_{a in S} sigma_i^a. In a diluted model the cavity insertion depends on all of them, so the structural route leaves a gap: one must also show that general states are approximated by finite-RSB ones.
lesson.lesson_statement: The object to control is the full family of finite multioverlaps on prescribed replica trees, not pair-overlap ultrametricity (C1).
lesson.summary_excerpt: pair-overlap ultrametricity alone does not determine the multioverlaps
lesson.generality: general (rules out every route through pair-overlap structure alone for diluted models)
lesson.known_in_literature: Known. Panchenko, 'Spin glass models from the point of view of spin distributions', Ann. Probab. 41 (2013) shows the diluted-model state is a spin distribution governed by all multioverlaps. The final paper (intro) repeats this point and cites Pan13; the trace does not cite Pan13.
lesson.salvage: The multioverlap R_S becomes the basic observable (paper eq. tree:multioverlap); Panchenko's hierarchical representation idea survives as the target shape of the trial law (comp:encoding).
lesson.influence: triggers the counterexample probe (restart 1); see a1
lesson.what_was_not_learned: The trace never says how to bridge from ultrametric pair structure to multioverlaps. It drops the 'identify the physical Gibbs structure' programme entirely and later builds the hierarchy into the construction (PV2). eureka_candidates.load_bearing: High. The decorrelation section (3384 of 14918 paper words, 23%) depends on it, and through Thm decor:overlap-concentration so do the comparison and the lower bound. The paper's introduction and overview single it out as the key step.
arguments_for: No precedent is named in the trace or in the paper (the paper names antecedents for the perturbation identities but none for the shift).
It is reached after a visible run of six failures, three of them explicit small-denominator failures, so the obvious variants (coarse partitions, equal-exponent refinements) were tried and failed.

Syntactically tiny (add 1 to every internal depth) yet it changes the proof budget qualitatively: without it, errors after division by kappa(S)^2 ~ delta^{2b} are uncontrolled; with it, a uniform constant C_{k,eta}. This is the Cook-Reckhow signature (small definition, large budget drop).
The model marks it with the only 'Great!' in the trace.
arguments_against: It is one step from the learned clause C10: once one knows that each fresh unary split costs delta and that the normalizer has one delta per branching vertex, forcing target splits to be fresh is a natural move. It is general position applied to tree depths.
It needs the model's own tree calculus (PV3) and a standard martingale averaging (PV6), so its value is local to this framework. The downstream speedup test may show it to be a one-off device.
Delaying or perturbing parameters to avoid degeneracies is a generic mathematical habit; a discovery test may find it easily once C10 is given in the prompt.
